notes.meaning: Moses lists the family lines that belonged to the tribe of Asher. These clans traced back to Asher's sons and grandsons. Even through decades of wandering in the desert, each family line remained distinct and recognized.

Asher's daughter Serah is singled out by name, just as she was when Jacob's family first went down to Egypt. It was rare for women to be named in ancient family registries, showing she was a prominent and well-remembered figure in Israel's history.

The men of Asher who were fit for military service totaled 53,400. This was an increase of nearly 12,000 men since the first count at Mount Sinai. God blessed this tribe with steady growth during the wilderness years.
Naphtali's tribe is recorded by its four main clans, which came from the sons born to Naphtali. These families preserved their tribal identity throughout their travels in the desert.

The fighting men of Naphtali numbered 45,400. This was 8,000 fewer men than at the first census forty years earlier. Some tribes grew while others shrank, reflecting the natural changes and losses during the journey.

The total number of fighting men across all the tribes came to 601,730. This was only 1,820 fewer men than the count at Mount Sinai forty years earlier. Even though the rebellious older generation had died off, God preserved the nation so it was ready to enter the land.

The Lord told Moses how the Promised Land was to be divided among the tribes. The land was to be given as an inheritance, meaning a permanent family possession, based on the census list. This gave the new generation full confidence that they would soon possess what God had promised.

God set down a fair rule for distributing the land. Larger tribes were to receive more territory, while smaller tribes were to receive less. Each tribe's share was to match the size of its population.

The general location of each tribe's land was to be decided by casting lots, while the size of the territory matched the tribe's numbers. Casting lots was a way of seeking God's direct guidance to prevent human jealousy and favoritism. This made it clear that God, as the true owner of the land, decided where each tribe would live.

The tribe of Levi was counted separately by its main branches: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari, along with their family groups. Levi was set apart for holy service rather than ordinary warfare. This list also highlights the family line of Amram, the father of Israel's great leaders.

Amram married Jochebed, who was also a descendant of Levi born in Egypt. She gave birth to Aaron the high priest, Moses the prophet, and their sister Miriam. God used this single family to lead and shape the entire nation.

Aaron had four sons who were set apart to serve as priests, but the two oldest, Nadab and Abihu, died when they offered unauthorized fire before the Lord. Their sudden deaths were a solemn reminder to treat God's worship with holy reverence. God preserved the priesthood through Aaron's younger sons, Eleazar and Ithamar.

The Levite males aged one month and older totaled 23,000. They were not counted with the fighting men because they did not receive a large territory like the other tribes. Instead of farming a region, their portion was the Lord's tabernacle service, and they were later given scattered towns to live in.

Moses and Eleazar the priest completed the census while Israel camped on the plains of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho. The camp stood on the very border of the Promised Land. Everything was now organized for the people to cross over and take the land.

Not one man from the Sinai census was left alive, except Caleb and Joshua. The Lord had warned that the rebellious generation would die in the wilderness, and His word was carried out completely. At the same time, God proved true to His promise by sparing Caleb and Joshua because they had trusted Him.
